title: Quarterly strategy for Dedicated capacity: SLA-driven autoscale, cost caps, and rollout milestones
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures the product roadmap and OKR alignment for the Q4 initiative to deliver SLA-driven autoscaling for Dedicated customers. The core outcome is a predictable, cost-capped autoscale experience that guarantees tail-latency SLOs for reserved capacity customers while minimizing waste and preserving contractual SLAs.

Goals / Success metrics (OKRs):
- Objective: Deliver a resilient autoscale model for Dedicated customers that supports 99th percentile latency SLO and a cost cap for reserved contracts.
  - KR1: End-to-end autoscale canary deployed to 3 pilot customers by 2025-11-30.
  - KR2: 99th percentile latency for autoscaled requests remains within 1.5x of reserved capacity baseline under 90th percentile load bursts (target: <=120ms increase for gen workloads).
  - KR3: Implement per-customer monthly cost cap controls and alerting; reduce autoscale over-provisioning by 25% vs baseline.
  - KR4: Complete docs and runbook for Dedicated capacity SRE & customer-facing playbook.

Scope and deliverables (quarter):
- Autoscale policy primitives: time-based, load-based (qps/p90), and predictive (short-horizon forecasting). Include cost-capping rules per customer.
- SLA enforcement layer: policy that maps SLAs -> min capacity reservation + fallback strategies (model variant fallback, region fallback, pre-warm capacity).
- Pricing toggle and billing metadata: ability for sales/finance to opt into cost-cap enforcement vs unlimited-burst contracts.
- Observability: per-tenant dashboards (latency, warmup time, autoscale events), token-level cost deltas for autoscale events, and alerting thresholds.
- Rollout plan: internal beta -> 3 pilot customers -> graduated availability for new Dedicated customers -> retrospective & iteration.

Key trade-offs discussed:
- Aggressiveness of predictive autoscale: more aggressive reduces latency but increases cost. Decision: default to conservative predictive scaling with opt-in aggressive mode for enterprise pilots.
- Cost cap enforcement vs availability: hard caps may reduce availability during extreme spikes; decision: implement soft cap with degradations (fallback to smaller model variant) and escalating alerts, plus an override flow for SRE/sales.
- Complexity vs time-to-market: prefer a phased approach with minimal viable policy primitives first (time/load/predictive), then add advanced multi-model routing later.

Owners & stakeholders:
- PM: Priya Shah (owner)
- Eng leads: Alex Kim (serving runtime), Mateo Rivera (orchestration), Sanjay Patel (billing)
- Design: Erin Brooks (console UX & dashboards)
- SRE/Ops: Jordan Lee (runbooks, canary ops)
- Sales/CS: Casey O'Neill (pilot coordination and contract language)

Milestones & timeline:
- Week 1-2 (2025-10-29 -> 2025-11-11): finalize PRD, define SLA mapping model, wireframes for per-tenant dashboard.
- Week 3-5 (2025-11-12 -> 2025-12-02): engineering deliverables: autoscale policy primitives implemented, basic telemetry emitted.
- Week 6 (2025-12-03 -> 2025-12-09): internal beta + SRE runbook dry-run.
- Week 7-8 (2025-12-10 -> 2025-12-19): pilot rollouts to 3 customers, collect metrics, iterate on thresholds.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Predictive autoscale models might underperform on unusual workloads. Mitigation: conservative defaults, immediate fallbacks to reserved capacity and model-variant routing.
- Risk: Billing mismatches when cost caps interact with burst pricing. Mitigation: enforce billing metadata tags and pre-deployment billing simulation for pilots.
- Risk: UX confusion on cost caps and override flows. Mitigation: clear console affordances and in-product confirmation dialogs; sales enablement materials.

Open decisions required from leadership:
- Acceptable latency delta at p99 for autoscaled vs reserved baseline (proposed: 1.5x at p99 for gen workloads).
- Policy for hard vs soft cost caps and who can override.

Artifacts & links:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated-autoscale-q4-prd (draft)
- Draft console mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/dedicated-autoscale-ui (v1)
- Pilot customer list & contracts: internal doc (link withheld, sales only)

Notes on cross-team engineering scope (for ENG handoff):
- Runtime: kernel selection for fast warmup paths, KV cache prefetch for pre-warmed instances.
- Orchestration: per-tenant scaling groups and quick signal propagation (sub-2s decision window).
- Billing: tagging autoscale events with billing reasons and cost attribution.
- Console: new dashboard panels for cap/usage, and billing tie-outs.

Acceptance criteria (for Done):
- Feature flags enabled with telemetry and runbook completed.
- 3 pilot customers successfully complete two-week pilot with agreed KR thresholds met.
- Billing simulations validated for pilot contracts.
- Documentation for SRE and customer-facing guides published.
